cases.evidence_note: Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (IRA Deduction Worksheet, Social Security Benefits Worksheet, Tax Table), p590a, f8606, i8606 and f8880, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding; recorded after comparison. Facts: Married filing jointly, both aged 39. You are covered by a plan at work; wages $66,000. Your spouse is not covered; wages $51,500. Taxable interest $9,000. Each of you contributes $7,000 to a traditional IRA. The two predictors differed here only on rounding: Pub. 590-A Example 1 prints $6,825, but its own Worksheet 1-2 line 4 ("If the result isn't a multiple of $10, round it to the next highest multiple of $10") and the i1040gi IRA Deduction Worksheet line 7 ("increase it to the next multiple of $10") give $6,830; the expected values follow the printed rule (predictor B), and the example's figure is an open owner question. Working (predictor B): 1040 line 9 = 66,000+51,500+9,000 = 126,500. WS (i1040gi p.97): 2a 146,000 (covered, MFJ); 2b 246,000 (not covered). 3 = 126,500; 4 = 0; 5 = 126,500 both. 6a = 19,500 (<20,000, covered column -> line 7); 6b = 119,500 (>=10,000, uncovered column -> 7b = 7,000). 7a = 19,500 x 0.35 = 6,825 -> next multiple of $10 = 6,830 (p.98 line 7). 8 = 117,500 wages; 9 = 0; 10 = 117,500. 11a = 11b = 7,000. 12a = min(6,830,117,500,7,000) = 6,830; 12b = 7,000. s1 line 20 = 13,830 = line 26. Form 8606 (you): line 1 = 7,000 - 6,830 = 170; line 2 = 0; line 3 = 170; no distribution/conversion -> line 14 = 170. AGI = 126,500 - 13,830 = 112,670. Std ded MFJ 31,500. Line 15 = 81,170. Tax Table MFJ 81,150-81,200 = 9,264. Line 17 = 0 so line 18 = 9,264. Saver's credit: AGI > 79,000, not available.

IRA Deduction Worksheet line 3 (Form 1040 line 9) $150,000; line 4 adds Schedule 1 line 18, $500; modified AGI for Roth purposes is line 5, $149,500 (i8606 p. 4, Modified AGI worksheet), below $150,000 (p590a p. 2), so no Roth screen refuses: Schedule 2 line 8 $0. Line 3 alone would be at the threshold.

Predicted by hand before evaluating: single, born 1985, W-2 $50,000, a traditional IRA contribution of $8,000 and no Roth contribution. The Roth screen person.ira_roth_over asks only about a person who made Roth contributions (p590a p. 43), so it is false here however far the traditional contribution exceeds the $7,000 limit.

Married filing jointly, wages $6,000 (taxpayer, born 1970) and $5,000 (spouse), a Roth IRA contribution of $3,000 by the taxpayer, none by the spouse, no traditional contributions. Worksheet line 10 is $11,000, under the $15,000 of the caution (one spouse 50 or older), which used to refuse every Roth contributor on such a return. p590a p. 10: the Kay Bailey Hutchison limit only raises the limit of the spouse with less compensation; the taxpayer's own limit is the smaller of $8,000 and $6,000 of compensation, and $3,000 is within it, and $3,000 is within the couple's $11,000. No excess, so no refusal.

Married filing jointly, wages $6,000 (taxpayer) and $5,000 (spouse), both under 50; the spouse contributes $5,500 to a Roth IRA, more than the spouse's own $5,000 of compensation. p590a p. 10, Kay Bailey Hutchison Spousal IRA Limit: the spouse's compensation is less than the taxpayer's, so the spouse's limit is the smaller of $7,000 and the couple's $11,000 less the taxpayer's contributions ($0), $7,000; $5,500 is within it. The spouse's compensation doubled ($10,000) is less than line 10 ($11,000), so the own-compensation test does not apply, and no refusal.

Married filing jointly, wages $6,000 (taxpayer, born 1970, so 50 or older) and $5,000 (spouse); the taxpayer contributes $6,500 to a Roth IRA. p590a p. 10: the Kay Bailey Hutchison limit applies only to a spouse whose compensation is less than the other's; the taxpayer's compensation is the larger, so the taxpayer's limit is the smaller of $8,000 and $6,000, and $500 is an excess contribution (p590a p. 43, the 6% tax of Form 5329 Part IV). Within the couple's $11,000 and within $8,000, so only the own-compensation test (twice $6,000 is at least line 10's $11,000, and $6,500 is more than $6,000) refuses Schedule 2 line 8 (person.x_tax) at person.ira_roth_over.
